subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram DMs can still land in agent:main:main, polluting heartbeat/main session after #40519

question: Should this issue be resolved narrowly by fixing heartbeat `session` precedence for system-event wakes, or should it also change the documented default Telegram DM-to-main routing policy?
rationale: Source inspection proves the heartbeat precedence bug, but current docs intentionally allow shared main-session DMs unless `dmScope` isolates them, so automation should not silently change that product policy.

options.title: Land narrow heartbeat fix
options.body: Adopt, rebase, or replace the linked implementation so configured heartbeat sessions win for system-event-triggered wakes while leaving documented Telegram DM defaults unchanged.

options.title: Split DM default policy
options.body: Keep this issue focused on heartbeat session pollution and use a separate issue for any proposal to change Telegram DM default isolation.

options.title: Close as intentional defaults
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide `dmScope` configuration is sufficient and the heartbeat-session precedence path no longer needs a code fix.

recommendation.title: Land narrow heartbeat fix
recommendation.body: Adopt, rebase, or replace the linked implementation so configured heartbeat sessions win for system-event-triggered wakes while leaving documented Telegram DM defaults unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: The current blame trail puts the central heartbeat, exec wake, and Telegram/session routing helpers under the most recent Vincent Koc-authored current-main refactor.
